name: AI trade jitters
backstory: Markets have leaned heavily on AI-linked mega-cap tech [the very largest companies by value], so doubts about AI spending or China competition hit the whole index. Last week brought a sharp AI selloff and warnings that the S&P 500 is dangerously exposed to AI. Nvidia's CEO exit then knocked its stock on Nov 12.
today: The earlier rebound reversed: the Nasdaq fell 2.49%. Chip stocks dropped on planned Commerce Department restrictions, Micron and AMD fell, rare-earth stocks sank, and the Nvidia board is reportedly not considering bringing Huang back. Fed Chairman Warsh said AI is important to the economy but could 'disappoint'. A Fed survey named AI risks the biggest threat to the financial system, and Governor Barr gave a speech on AI and financial stability. ECB Vice-President Vujčić said the risk of an AI market repricing has 'further increased'.

name: Central banks vs energy inflation
backstory: The Iran war cut oil supply and lifted headline inflation. Central banks must judge whether it fades or leaks into wages and services, and after 2021 they are less willing to wait. Lagarde said euro-area inflation hit 4% in October, and the Bank of England hiked to 4% last week.
today: US numbers are hot: October consumer prices rose 0.4%, more than expected, and wholesale prices rose 0.3% in the month for an annual 6.5%, the highest in nearly four years. A 'jumbo' hike debate is brewing for the December Fed meeting, and the dollar hit its highest since April 2025 on hike bets. Vujčić said euro-area inflation rose to 4% from 3.8%, wages are not responding materially yet, and rising borrowing costs should partly contain inflation. A French central bank speech noted yields have risen across advanced economies since summer on the war, hike expectations and heavy bond issuance. Japan's economy shrank in Q3 as energy costs bit.

name: Iran war and oil
backstory: The conflict that began in early 2026 cut global oil output by 12 mb/d [million barrels per day] in March. Prices jumped but not to records, because the world was oversupplied before and stored oil filled the gap. Tensions eased in June and then returned.
today: WTI fell 3.95% to 85.06 as recovering Middle East exports strengthened the surplus outlook. Energy stocks retreated, and Canada's TSX dropped 380 points as metal and energy stocks slid. Yet Vujčić says the ongoing war is still pushing energy prices up in Europe, so the inflation effect has not vanished.

name: Yen defense
backstory: A weak yen pushed Japan to intervene [sell dollars to buy yen] in the foreign exchange market, including a record $50 billion in one day. The Bank of Japan's 1.25% rate is far below the Fed's 3.875%, a gap of 2.625 percentage points, which encourages selling yen to hold dollars.
today: Japan's Q3 economy unexpectedly contracted as elevated energy costs bit. A headline says the dollar rally and Japan's slump leave the yen under pressure, though USD/JPY slipped 0.28% to 159.43 today. A hawkish [favoring higher rates] BOJ policymaker, Takata, called for a swift hike.

name: US midterms and the dollar
backstory: The midterms produced what headlines call a Democratic rout, with voters blaming Trump for economic pain. Markets are asking how divided government would change tariffs, spending and the dollar.
today: The dollar index fell 0.19% and gold is up about 4% since the vote. HSBC says strong Democratic results could pressure the dollar near term, and the NZ dollar rose after the election. One analysis says Democrats have one chance to extract concessions from Trump and markets will dislike it, another explains how they might try to end tariffs, and both sides are trading threats of investigations.
